content: May the Sugatas of the ten directions and four times, together with their heirs,Who embody the wisdom body and maintain the manner of non-duality,Within the state of equanimity of the youthful Mañjuśrī,Spontaneously accomplish the meaning of non-action.To the glorious guru, the primordial protector,With the devotion that views him as the dharmakāya of equanimity,May the blessings of the ultimate lineage be transferred to my heart,And may I obtain the great empowerment of the creative power of awareness.Because it is primordially present, it is not accomplished through effort,And though it does not depend on differences in capacity and the like,Because it is so simple, one does not believe it—this is the secret of the mind;May it be seen through the power of the guru’s pith instructions.Conceptual elaboration and analysis are but additional fabrications of thought,Seeking and striving are causes for one's own exhaustion,Focusing and meditating are cages that further bind;May the elaborations of such afflictive pain be cut from within.Although it is beyond thought and expression, with nothing to be seen,There is nothing remaining that has not been seen;This is the profound meaning of reaching certainty in one's own mind;May this reality, so difficult to indicate, be realized.Since all conceptual elaboration is pure from the very beginning, the extreme of existence is abandoned.Because the radiance of awareness is spontaneously present, it is free from the extreme of nihilism.Although spoken of as two, this is merely the way the conceptual mind engages;May we see the meaning of equality—indivisible and ineffable!Just as a finger points to the moon,Although initially indicated by words and intellectual investigation,The natural state is beyond the reach of conceptual thought;May it be seen by looking into itself!In this, there is nothing to be removed,And not the slightest thing to be added or established;Within the state of reality, unpolluted by the effort of rejection or realization,May we enter into the meaning of spontaneous presence!Though we designate a ground of what is to be known, a path to be traversed,And the qualities of a result to be attained,In their natural disposition, they are like the stages of space;May we spontaneously abide in the meaning of non-action!Impure saṃsāric phenomena, conceived in delusion,And even the pure appearances that are the reverse of those,Are dependent designations, elaborate projections;May we see that they do not abide within the non-elaborated natural state!Within the way the dharmatā, the natural state, abides—free from the conceptual mind—Obscured by conceptual thought, it is tainted by viewing and meditating.Arriving at the ordinary natural state, free from viewing and meditating,May we naturally remain in the genuine condition!To focus on anything is the poison of the view,Whatever is held with effort is the defect of meditation,Adopting and avoiding are the narrow pass of conduct;May we see the dharmatā, free from all such pain!The radiance of awareness, not caught in the cage of conceptual elaboration,Is seen directly, beyond the mind; may we not, through intellectual speculation,Cast a noose to tie a knot in the sky,But become skilled in the meaning of genuine natural rest!At that time, the youthful vase body of self-knowing awareness,The Mañjughoṣa of natural luminosity,Through the appearance of the lamp of self-arisen wisdom,Banish the dense darkness of mind’s obscurations!In the nature, which is uncompounded and uncontrived,Since nothing is newly accomplished through fabricated paths,May we see the meaning of the ultimate fruition, which does not arise from causes,As that which has been primordially present within ourselves!The path of delusion is the chaff of words and intellectual speculation;However they are expressed, they are but a web of conceptual thought.May we meditate in our hearts on the profound instructionsThat do not arise from scripture, but are to be personally realized!The mind of subject and object is deluded by its very nature;Whatever is observed is not suchness itself.May we attain the buddhahood of definitive reality,The self-arisen wisdom body that does not arise from the mind!Within the expanse of awareness, the unity of awareness and emptiness, all phenomenaBecome equal in the single, unique sphere;In that state where hopes and fears for saṃsāra and nirvāṇa have collapsed,May we capture the permanent stronghold of the non-abiding dharmakāya!Whatever we perceive, as the body or as objects of the senses,Is like defective vision, apparent through the force of thought alone;By means of the natural radiance of great, non-conceptual wisdom,May all be purified into the original space of phenomenal exhaustion!At that time, may the wisdom body, vast as space,Throughout all directions and times, for as long as existence lasts,Be a wish-fulfilling jewel that grants every benefit and happiness to all beings,And may the ultimate fruition, free from all obscurations, be attained!This was written to completion by Mi-pham 'Jam-dpal-dgyes-pa, also known as 'Od-gsal-rdo-rje, on an auspicious day in the Fire-Dog year (1886, when he was 41), at the request of the venerable Bde-skyong-ye-shes-dbang-mo—widely renowned as an emanation of Jñāna-ḍākinī-vārāhī—who offered a blessed silk scarf and a precious white crystal rosary; through the merit of having spoken whatever arose, in the unique and independent language of the Great Perfection tradition, may all beings attain the state of the primordial protector, the youthful Mañjuśrī. As the Vajradhara has praised this supreme path, saying that merely hearing it brings certain liberation, what need is there to mention the benefit of contemplating its meaning? By the truth of the nature of phenomena, may one be quickly liberated. When it is difficult to tame beings through the paths involving effort, may the essence of the teachings, as praised in the prophecies of the appearance of the Kuntuzangpo heart-mind teachings, spread and flourish throughout the world. Sarvamaṅgalam.
